desc: Analyze the cost formula: cost([l, r]) = sum_{i=l}^{r} (max(nums[l..i]) - nums[i]) = (sum of running maxes) - (sum of elements).
Discard the segment tree approach (too slow with O(n log^3 n) or memory-heavy) in favor of the O(n) two-pointer stack approach.

Implement sliding window with a stack of (value, length, sum_nums) segments; add-right is O(1) amortized via merging; remove-left is O(1) if the leftmost element is not the global max for the first segment, else O(1) pop and adjust; maintain total_vlen and total_sum; cost = total_vlen - total_sum.
Iterate r from 0 to n-1, expanding the window by adding nums[r]; while cost > k, shrink l by 1 (remove-left). Add (r - l + 1) to the answer.
Verify on the two examples: nums=[6,3,1,2,4,4], k=7 → 17; nums=[6,3,1,3,6], k=4 → 12.
Test edge cases: n=1; k very large (all subarrays valid); k very small (only single-element subarrays valid).
If the O(1) remove-left is incorrect, fall back to a segment tree with O(log n) merge using prefix sums on segment lists (but optimized to avoid O(n) list copies).
